confidence: medium-high — an introductory survey of five religions, an in-depth study of two through five themes, and an investigative study; this course is SL only
note: Three levels: part of the course, unit, then one assessable point.

subtopics: What counts as a religion and how religions are studied
Comparing religions fairly and avoiding stereotype
The three fundamental questions: condition, destiny, path
Hinduism: origins, beliefs, texts and practice
Buddhism: the Buddha, the four noble truths and the path
Sikhism: the Gurus, the Guru Granth Sahib and practice
Judaism: covenant, Torah, practice and festivals
Christianity: Jesus, scripture, denominations and worship
Islam: the Qur'an, the five pillars and the Sunni-Shia distinction
Baha'i faith and Zoroastrianism: teachings and practice
Taoism: the Tao, wu wei and practice
New religious movements and secular worldviews
Daily, weekly and annual ritual cycles
Rites of passage: birth, initiation, marriage, death
Genres within scripture: law, narrative, poetry, prophecy
Scripture in worship: recitation, memorisation and liturgy
Ultimate reality: God, gods, no-self or emptiness
Cosmology, creation and the end of things
Salvation, liberation and the human condition
Sources of moral authority: text, reason, tradition, community
Applied ethics: life, sexuality, war and wealth
Social ethics: justice, charity and compassion
Choosing a focused religious question or practice
Selecting sources: texts, interviews and observation
Ethical and respectful engagement with a community
Describing the practice or belief accurately
Analysing meaning and significance for believers
Reflecting on what was learned and its limits
